s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lower lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
Auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways

shortlist.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of facial asymmetry with abnormal lower lip movement

shortlist.label: Asymmetric crying face syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by abnormal movement of the lower lip during crying, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Congenital unilateral agenesis of the depressor anguli oris muscle
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to congenital unilateral hypoplasia, this condition could explain the patient's lower lip deviation

shortlist.label: Unilateral congenital lower lip pit
shortlist.why_kept: Could be related to the abnormal lower lip movement, although less directly connected to the primary symptom

shortlist.label: Congenital lower lip sinuses
shortlist.why_kept: Another condition that might explain the lower lip abnormalities, although less common and less directly connected

raw.rationale: The key fact that the right lower lip deviates inward when the child smiles or cries, with otherwise symmetric facial movement, is most consistent with asymmetric crying face syndrome, which is characterized by an abnormal appearance of the mouth during crying due to weakness of the depressor anguli oris muscle on one side.

rejected.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris
rejected.why: While this condition could explain the facial asymmetry, asymmetric crying face syndrome is a more specific diagnosis that matches the described symptoms.

rejected.label: Congenital unilateral agenesis of the depressor anguli oris muscle
rejected.why: This condition would likely result in more pronounced facial asymmetry and potentially other symptoms, which are not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Unilateral congenital lower lip pit
rejected.why: The presence of a lip pit was not mentioned in the vignette, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Congenital lower lip sinuses
rejected.why: Similar to the unilateral congenital lower lip pit, there is no mention of sinuses, making this an unlikely diagnosis.
